source_meta._title: Horses' armor, reins, and bridles experience z-fighting

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition Minecraft 1.14.2 in a single-player world using the integrated server. Use a Creative-mode world with cheats enabled as the simplest practical environment for executing the supplied summon command. Use keyboard and mouse controls; key names below assume the default bindings. The report specifies no seed, coordinates, resource pack, graphics preset, shader, or dedicated-server requirement.
preconditions: Install or configure a Minecraft: Java Edition installation/profile for Minecraft 1.14.2, the first version listed as affected.
Do not use 23w14a for this reproduction because the report lists it as the fix version rather than an affected version.
Create or load a single-player world in Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled. Creative mode is an execution convenience; the report does not specify a required game mode.
Wait until the surrounding terrain has rendered and movement, camera rotation, and chat input respond normally.
Move to a well-lit, open area with enough unobstructed space to stand near and view a horse from the front and sides.
If controls are rebound, use the bindings for Open Chat, Change Perspective, Use Item/Place Block, and Sneak/Dismount in place of the default T, F5, right-click, and Left Shift inputs.

steps.action: Launch the installation/profile configured for Minecraft: Java Edition Minecraft 1.14.2, then enter the prepared single-player world.
steps.success_cue: The world is open in Minecraft 1.14.2 and the player can move and rotate the camera normally.

steps.action: Wait at the open test location until nearby chunks and entity rendering have finished loading. Do not begin while the terrain is visibly appearing or input is delayed.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is fully rendered, the frame updates normally, and movement responds without loading pauses.

steps.action: Set the camera to first-person perspective so later F5 perspective changes are deterministic. Press the Change Perspective key repeatedly, if necessary, until the player's own body is not shown in front of the camera.
steps.exact_input: F5 until first-person perspective is active
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is centered on the world and the player's full character model is not visible in front of the camera.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat key to open the in-game chat and command input. The command must be run by the player in chat, with the leading slash included.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept text.

steps.action: Enter the report's summon command exactly as supplied, including capitalization, quotation marks, braces, commas, namespace identifiers, count values, and the leading slash. Press Enter once to execute it.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a syntax or permission error, and a horse appears at or immediately beside the player's position wearing diamond horse armor and a saddle.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so the player is not holding an item that could perform a different interaction. The hotbar is the row of nine slots along the bottom of the gameplay screen; press the number key corresponding to an empty slot.
steps.exact_input: Press a number key from 1 through 9 corresponding to an empty hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: No held item is visible in the player's hand.

steps.action: Move a short distance away if the horse spawned intersecting the player, then approach it until the crosshair can be placed on the center of its torso. Release all movement keys before interacting.
steps.exact_input: Use W/A/S/D as needed; center the crosshair on the horse's torso
steps.success_cue: The horse is fully visible at close interaction distance, is not obstructed by blocks, and the crosshair rests on its torso.

steps.action: Use the horse once to mount it. With default controls, right-click the horse while the crosshair is on its torso. Do not open the horse inventory or remove its saddle or armor.
steps.success_cue: The viewpoint rises into the riding position and the riding HUD, such as the horse health and jump indicators, confirms that the player is mounted on the horse.

steps.action: Release all movement controls and allow the mounted horse and camera to become stationary before changing perspective.
steps.exact_input: Release W, A, S, D, Space, and sprint controls
steps.success_cue: The mounted horse is not being deliberately moved or made to jump, and the camera is stable enough for close visual inspection.

steps.action: Switch from first-person to rear third-person perspective so the mounted player, horse, saddle, armor, and reins can be viewed externally.
steps.success_cue: The camera is behind the mounted player and the horse's equipped body and head are visible in the same frame.

steps.action: Use the mouse to angle the third-person camera toward the horse's head and upper neck. Frame the reins closely enough that the strips extending between the horse's bridle area and the rider can be inspected. Keep the horse stationary and hold the view until the camera has rendered several stable frames.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse to frame the horse's reins; do not press movement keys
steps.success_cue: The reins and their connection near the horse's head and neck are visible and unobstructed in a stable mounted view.

steps.action: Press the Change Perspective key once more to enter front-facing third-person perspective. Angle the camera slightly downward as needed and frame at least one side of the horse's neck directly below the reins. Hold the resulting viewpoint for several stable rendered frames.
steps.exact_input: F5 once, then move the mouse to frame one side of the neck below the reins
steps.success_cue: The camera faces the mounted player and horse, with the armor and the neck surface immediately below at least one rein visible without block obstruction.

steps.action: Dismount the horse while it still has the summoned saddle and diamond horse armor equipped. With default controls, press the Sneak/Dismount key once; do not attack the horse or open its inventory.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing independently beside the horse, while the same horse remains nearby with its saddle and diamond horse armor equipped.

steps.action: Return to first-person perspective. Because the previous view was front-facing third-person, press F5 once under the default perspective cycle. If the perspective cycle differs, continue only until the player's full model is no longer visible in front of the camera.
steps.exact_input: F5 once, or until first-person perspective is active
steps.success_cue: The camera is in first-person perspective and the dismounted horse remains nearby.

steps.action: Move approximately one to three blocks from the horse, turn toward its head, and center the view on the bridle around its face and muzzle. Adjust the angle only enough to keep the bridle, adjacent armor, and both sides of the head unobstructed; then stop moving and hold the view for several stable rendered frames.
steps.exact_input: Use W/A/S/D and the mouse as needed; center the crosshair near the horse's bridle
steps.success_cue: The player is dismounted and stationary at close viewing distance, with the equipped horse's head and bridle centered and clearly visible.

stor.handoff_condition: The horse has just been mounted in step 8 with its summoned saddle and diamond horse armor still equipped. Begin continuous visual observation at this mounted state, retain observation while the executor frames the reins and neck in steps 10 through 12, and continue through the dismount and final bridle framing in steps 13 through 15. The final state is a stationary first-person close view of the dismounted horse's head and bridle.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a required game mode, world seed, coordinates, world type, graphics setting, resource pack, camera perspective, or lighting condition. Creative mode, a fresh open area, and third-person mounted views are practical execution choices rather than report-stated requirements.

The report contains multiple visual inspection transitions: mounting the horse for the reins, framing the neck below the reins, and dismounting for the bridle. Because the output permits only one trigger_step, step 8 is selected as the earliest trigger and observation should continue through the later viewpoints and dismount.

The exact camera distance and viewing angle are not specified. The plan uses stable, unobstructed third-person mounted views and a close first-person dismounted view to operationalize 'look closely' without changing the horse or supplied command.
The summon command is preserved verbatim from the report and was not modified or independently web-verified.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 using the vanilla client and default vanilla resources, in a local single-player Creative-mode world with cheats enabled. A Superflat world and an elevated stone support are used as practical choices to make the comparator easy to approach from every direction.
preconditions: Use Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2, the first version listed as affected in the report.
Disable any resource pack that replaces or modifies redstone comparator block models or textures; use the vanilla resource pack for the model under test.
Use a single-player Creative-mode world with cheats enabled so the comparator and support blocks can be obtained without crafting and Spectator mode can be entered by command.
Keep the test comparator isolated from levers, redstone blocks, powered redstone dust, repeaters, comparators, or other possible sources of redstone input.
Use first-person view. Default keyboard and mouse controls are assumed; use the corresponding bound controls if they have been changed.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and start an installation configured for Java Edition 1.15.2. Wait for the title screen to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is visible and identifies the running version as 1.15.2.

steps.action: Create a local test world. From the title screen, open Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, and select the Superflat world type. Confirm the options and create the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options... -> Allow Cheats: ON -> World Type: Superflat -> Done -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: World generation begins with Creative mode and commands enabled.

steps.action: Wait before interacting until the player has spawned, nearby terrain has rendered, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the loaded world and can move without waiting for terrain generation.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory control, which is E by default, and select the Search Items tab identified by the compass icon.
steps.exact_input: E; then click the Search Items tab
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory search field and searchable item grid are visible.

steps.action: Click the search field, search for stone, and place one stack of the ordinary Stone block into hotbar slot 1. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 contains Stone.

steps.action: Replace the search text with comparator, locate the item named Redstone Comparator, and place it into hotbar slot 2.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 2 contains a Redstone Comparator while slot 1 still contains Stone.

steps.action: Close the Creative inventory using E or Escape and move to an open area with no existing redstone components nearby.
steps.exact_input: E or Escape; then W/A/S/D as needed
steps.success_cue: The normal first-person world view is visible and there is clear ground available for an isolated support pillar.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 1, aim at an exposed top face of the ground, and use the place-block control, which is right-click by default, once to place the first Stone support block.
steps.success_cue: One Stone block has been placed on top of the ground.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of the Stone block just placed and right-click once more to add a second Stone block above it, producing a two-block-high isolated pillar.
steps.success_cue: A two-block-high Stone pillar stands in open space with air around its sides.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 2, aim at the top face of the upper Stone block, and right-click once to place the Redstone Comparator on the pillar.
steps.success_cue: A Redstone Comparator is resting on top of the Stone pillar.

steps.action: Leave the comparator in the state created by its initial placement. Do not right-click the comparator again, and do not place any redstone power source or input component next to it.
steps.success_cue: The comparator remains isolated, receives no rear or side redstone input, and has not been toggled after placement.

steps.action: Press T to open the in-game chat interface so a game-mode command can be executed.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to receive a command.

steps.action: Enter the Spectator-mode command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted, command feedback identifies Spectator mode, and the player can fly and pass through blocks.

steps.action: Using Spectator flight, approach the comparator from one side. Use W, A, S, and D for horizontal movement, Space to rise, Left Shift to descend, and the mouse to look around. Stop just outside the comparator at approximately the height where its three torch elements emerge from the base.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D; Space; Left Shift; mouse movement
steps.success_cue: The camera is immediately beside the comparator and the three torch elements can be used as spatial reference points.

steps.action: Fly forward through the side of the comparator model. Adjust the camera vertically until its viewpoint is inside the comparator base and below the three torch elements, then pitch the view upward so the underside regions of the torch elements are centered. Use small movement adjustments to avoid passing completely through the model.
steps.exact_input: W or the appropriate horizontal movement key; Space/Left Shift for small vertical adjustments; move the mouse upward to look toward the torch undersides
steps.success_cue: The Spectator camera is clipped inside the unpowered comparator, positioned beneath its torch elements, with the underside regions of those elements centered for inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is in Spectator mode and the camera has just been positioned inside the isolated, unpowered comparator beneath its three torch elements, looking upward at their underside regions. Begin model-face observation without changing the comparator state or camera position.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, terrain type, support-block arrangement, or comparator orientation. A Superflat Creative world and a two-block-high Stone pillar are practical execution choices that preserve the reported requirement of placing an unpowered comparator while making spectator-camera positioning easier.

The report does not provide exact camera coordinates or viewing angles. The final position must therefore be adjusted based on the rendered model until the camera is inside the comparator base and below the torch elements.
The report does not explicitly specify whether custom resource packs were active. This plan uses vanilla resources because the report identifies the affected vanilla comparator model files.
No external verification was needed because the report supplies the required edition, affected versions, target block state, game mode, and triggering camera action.
